overview.title: Expert Emergency Care,  Anytime You Need It
overview.subtitle: At Narayana Health, we recognise that medical emergencies can happen anytime without warning and without an appointment. There might be a sudden cardiac arrest, a traumatic injury, as in a car crash, a stroke, a massive internal bleed, a complication of pregnancy, or a child in distress. Whether it's an acute emergency or not, our staff are trained for prompt response.

items.title: Road traffic accidents & polytrauma
items.text:
Severe multi-injury cases are stabilised using standard trauma protocols and close monitoring. The team initiates polytrauma resuscitation and coordinates imaging and specialist care as needed.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Industrial/workplace injuries, crush injuries
items.text:
These injuries may involve deep tissue damage, bleeding, fractures, or nerve and vessel compromise. Emergency care focuses on pain control, wound management, and rapid escalation if surgery is required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Head trauma & concussion
items.text:
Head trauma may cause headache, vomiting, dizziness, or brief confusion after an injury. We assess neurological status and arrange imaging when indicated to rule out internal injury.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Head injury with loss of consciousness
items.text:
Loss of consciousness after injury is treated as a medical priority even if external wounds appear small. We stabilise airway and circulation, then proceed with urgent neurological assessment and scans as indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Fractures and dislocations
items.text:
Fractures and dislocations can cause severe pain, swelling, deformity and restricted movement. We provide immobilisation and pain relief, including dislocation reduction, splinting/casting, POP applications, when required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Spine injuries / paraplegia (suspected spinal cord injury)
items.text:
Spine trauma may present with severe neck/back pain, weakness, numbness or loss of control. We immobilise early and coordinate urgent imaging and specialist management to protect function.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Minor burns / scalds
items.text:
Burns and scalds are assessed for depth, area involved and risk of infection. We provide burn first aid, dressings and pain control, with escalation when required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Electric shock
items.text:
Electric injuries can affect the heart rhythm and internal tissues even when skin marks are minimal. We monitor ECG and vitals, assess for hidden injury, and treat complications promptly.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Trauma due to falls
items.text:
Falls can lead to fractures, head injury or internal injury, especially in older adults. Emergency evaluation includes stabilisation, pain control and imaging as clinically indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Chest trauma with breathing compromise
items.text:
Chest injuries can cause breathlessness, chest pain and reduced oxygen levels. We stabilise breathing and may perform needle thoracentesis or ICD insertion when indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Severe pain after trauma
items.text:
Severe pain can limit breathing and movement and may delay recovery if not controlled early. We use stepwise pain management including nerve blocks for selected injuries.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Airway compromise in trauma
items.text:
Airway compromise requires immediate assessment to protect breathing and oxygen delivery. Support may include endotracheal intubation or surgical airway insertion when required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Acute chest pain
items.text:
Chest pain can have cardiac and non-cardiac causes that require urgent evaluation. We perform rapid ECG-based assessment and start treatment based on findings.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Heart attack
items.text:
A heart attack occurs when blood flow to the heart muscle is reduced or blocked. We activate time-sensitive pathways and initiate treatment including thrombolysis where indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Cardiac arrest & emergency resuscitation
items.text:
Cardiac arrest needs immediate resuscitation to restore circulation and protect organs. Our teams follow advanced protocols and escalate for ECMO/IABP initiation in selected cases.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Heart failure–related emergencies
items.text:
Heart failure emergencies can present with sudden breathlessness, swelling or fluid overload. We stabilise breathing and circulation and shift to ICU care when clinically required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Life-threatening rhythm disturbances
items.text:
Serious rhythm problems may cause palpitations, dizziness, fainting or sudden collapse. We provide monitoring and stabilisation and may initiate TPI where indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Pericardial tamponade suspicion
items.text:
Pericardial tamponade can cause low blood pressure, breathlessness and rapid deterioration. Urgent assessment is done and pericardiocentesis is performed when clinically required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Stroke (ischaemic and haemorrhagic)
items.text:
Stroke occurs due to a blocked vessel or bleeding in the brain and needs urgent action. We perform rapid imaging and initiate treatment including stroke fibrinolysis where indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Transient ischaemic attack (TIA)
items.text:
A TIA causes temporary stroke-like symptoms that resolve but can be a warning sign. Emergency care focuses on urgent evaluation and early prevention steps based on findings.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Seizures / fits
items.text:
Seizures may present with convulsions, staring episodes, confusion or loss of awareness. We ensure safety, control ongoing seizures when needed, and evaluate possible triggers.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Febrile seizures
items.text:
Febrile seizures can occur in children with a rapid rise in temperature during illness. We stabilise the child, manage fever, and assess for warning signs needing further care.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Head injuries with altered sensorium / unconsciousness
items.text:
Altered sensorium after head injury can indicate bleeding, swelling or brain involvement. We prioritise airway protection, neurological monitoring and urgent imaging as indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Raised intracranial pressure / hydrocephalus (selected cases)
items.text:
Some neurological emergencies require urgent pressure management to protect the brain. We stabilise the patient and may support neurosurgical intervention including EVD where indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

conditions.title: Breathing and Airway and Allergy Emergencies

items.title: Severe asthma or breathing issues
items.text:
Severe asthma can cause chest tightness, wheeze and difficulty breathing that may not settle at home. We start rapid inhalation therapy, oxygen support and close monitoring for escalation.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Cough, stridor, wheezing & breathlessness
items.text:
These symptoms may indicate airway narrowing, infection or allergic causes depending on age and severity. We assess quickly and initiate targeted respiratory support without delay.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Choking / foreign body aspiration
items.text:
Choking can partially or completely block the airway and needs urgent attention. We manage airway safety first and coordinate specialist support for removal when required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Anaphylactic shock
items.text:
Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that can cause swelling, breathing difficulty and low blood pressure. Emergency care includes immediate stabilisation, emergency medications and observation as needed.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Respiratory failure requiring ventilatory support
items.text:
Severe respiratory distress may require assisted breathing to stabilise oxygen and carbon dioxide levels. We initiate non-invasive or invasive ventilation and oxygen support including HFNO as indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Difficult airway situations
items.text:
Some patients require advanced airway planning to secure breathing safely. We provide difficult airway management and intubation as needed with continuous monitoring.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Ear-related emergencies
items.text:
Ear emergencies may involve severe pain, bleeding, infection complications or sudden symptoms. We provide focused assessment, pain control and timely ENT support when required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Foreign body removal & management (ear/nose/throat)
items.text:
Foreign bodies can cause pain, bleeding, infection or breathing difficulty depending on location. Safe removal is done using scope/device-guided techniques when needed.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Acute abdominal / stomach pain
items.text:
Sudden abdominal pain can be due to infection, inflammation, stones or surgical conditions. We evaluate promptly with examination, tests and imaging to guide treatment.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Colic pain & griping
items.text:
Colicky pain often comes in waves and may be related to bowel spasm or stones. We provide pain relief and assess the underlying cause through clinical evaluation.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Bowel obstruction
items.text:
Bowel obstruction can cause severe pain, vomiting, bloating and inability to pass stool or gas. We stabilise with fluids, urgent imaging and surgical review as required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Gastrointestinal bleeding (vomiting blood / blood in stool / bloody diarrhoea)
items.text:
Bleeding may range from mild to significant and can cause weakness or dizziness. We stabilise first, assess severity through tests, and involve specialists as indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Urine retention
items.text:
Urine retention can cause severe lower abdominal discomfort and pressure. We relieve obstruction promptly, including suprapubic catheterisation when indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Blocked urinary catheter
items.text:
A blocked catheter can lead to pain, leakage and urine backflow with infection risk. Emergency care restores drainage safely and assesses for infection or underlying cause.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Kidney stones
items.text:
Kidney stones commonly cause sudden severe flank pain with nausea or blood in urine. We provide pain relief and arrange imaging when needed to confirm size and location.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Kidney infection / pyelonephritis
items.text:
This infection can cause fever, flank pain, burning urination and weakness. We assess severity and start treatment promptly, with admission if clinically required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Haematuria (blood in urine)
items.text:
Blood in urine may occur due to infection, stones, injury or other urinary conditions. We evaluate the cause and manage clots, pain or blockage if present.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Kidney-related emergencies (fluid overload, emergency dialysis)
items.text:
Severe kidney problems can lead to breathlessness and dangerous fluid build-up. We stabilise first and coordinate emergency dialysis initiation when clinically required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Diabetic emergencies (low sugar / high sugar)
items.text:
Very low or very high sugar can cause sweating, confusion, dehydration or collapse. We correct glucose safely and evaluate triggers to reduce recurrence risk.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
items.text:
DKA is a serious complication that can cause vomiting, dehydration, rapid breathing and drowsiness. We initiate protocol-based management with fluids, insulin and monitoring.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Electrolyte imbalance (K/Na/Ca, Acidosis)
items.text:
Electrolyte disturbances can affect heart rhythm, muscles and brain function. We identify the cause and correct levels carefully with continuous monitoring.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Sepsis
items.text:
Sepsis is a serious body-wide response to infection that can affect blood pressure and organ function. We prioritise early recognition, rapid stabilisation and timely antibiotics.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Febrile neutropenia (immunocompromised fever)
items.text:
In patients with low immunity, fever can be an emergency even when symptoms are mild. We start urgent evaluation and early treatment with close monitoring as indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: All emergencies related to pregnancy
items.text:
Pregnancy emergencies may involve pain, bleeding, reduced foetal movements or sudden symptoms. We prioritise maternal and foetal assessment and coordinate urgent obstetric support.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage
items.text:
These conditions can present with pain and bleeding and may require urgent intervention. We stabilise the patient and proceed with tests, scans and obstetric management.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Pre-eclampsia & eclampsia emergencies
items.text:
These are high blood pressure emergencies in pregnancy that can affect brain and organs. We initiate rapid stabilisation including seizure control and urgent obstetric escalation.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Poisoning, trauma, or falls
items.text:
Children may accidentally ingest substances or suffer injuries during play and falls. We provide rapid assessment, stabilisation and age-appropriate monitoring and treatment.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Breathing difficulty, choking, dehydration, severe illness
items.text:
Paediatric breathing and hydration issues can worsen quickly without timely support. We provide early respiratory support and fluids as needed, with paediatric input when required.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Seizures and febrile seizures
items.text:
Seizures in children may occur with fever or other triggers and need prompt assessment. We stabilise the child, manage fever, and evaluate for warning signs.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Poisoning / toxic exposure
items.text:
Poisoning may affect breathing, consciousness and heart rhythm depending on the substance. We stabilise first and may use gastric lavage and poison-specific antidotes when indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Snake bites
items.text:
Snake bites can cause swelling, bleeding tendency, weakness or breathing difficulty. We assess severity and initiate protocol-based care including antivenom where indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Dog bite / animal bite
items.text:
Animal bites carry infection risk and may require tetanus and rabies prevention measures. We provide wound cleaning, vaccination guidance and antibiotics when indicated.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Bee sting / scorpion sting
items.text:
Stings can cause pain and swelling, and in some cases severe allergic reactions. We treat symptoms promptly and monitor closely when allergy risk is present.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Tumour bleeding
items.text:
Tumour-related bleeding can present as visible bleeding or sudden weakness and anaemia. We stabilise, control bleeding, and coordinate urgent oncology support based on severity.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Malignant spinal cord compression (MSCC)
items.text:
MSCC can cause back pain, weakness, numbness and bladder/bowel changes. We prioritise urgent assessment and imaging and initiate specialist management quickly.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: SVCS (Superior vena cava syndrome)
items.text:
SVCS may cause facial swelling, breathlessness and prominent chest veins due to vein compression. We stabilise the patient and start urgent specialist evaluation and treatment.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: DIC (Disseminated intravascular coagulation)
items.text:
DIC is a serious clotting and bleeding disorder seen in critical illness, infection or cancer. We initiate close monitoring and supportive care while treating the underlying cause.

Call 1800 309 0309

items.title: Phimosis & paraphimosis
items.text:
In men, the foreskin-related conditions can cause pain, swelling and difficulty passing urine. We provide urgent relief and pain control, with urology support as required.

Call 1800 309 0309

procedures.title: Emergency Medicine & Critical Care (Airway, Monitoring, Lines)

items.title: Endotracheal Intubation
items.text: A breathing tube is placed to keep the airway open and support breathing in critical situations.

items.title: Difficult Airway Management
items.text: Advanced airway methods are used to secure breathing safely when intubation is challenging.

items.title: Central Venous Catheter (CVC) Insertion
items.text: A central line is placed to give urgent medicines and fluids and support close monitoring.

items.title: Arterial Line Cannulation
items.text: An arterial line enables continuous blood pressure monitoring and accurate blood sampling.

items.title: Suprapubic Catheterisation
items.text: A small tube is placed directly into the bladder when urine drainage is urgently needed and routine catheterisation is not possible.

items.title: Invasive Ventilation (Ventilator) Initiation
items.text: Ventilator support is started when breathing is not adequate or safe.

items.title: Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV) Initiation
items.text: Mask-based ventilation supports breathing and improves oxygen levels without a tube.

items.title: HFNO Initiation
items.text: High-flow oxygen is given to improve oxygen levels and reduce breathing difficulty.

items.title: Oxygen Delivery Devices
items.text: Oxygen support is started early using the most suitable device for the patient’s condition.

items.title: Cardiac Arrest Resuscitation
items.text: Immediate resuscitation is provided to restore heartbeat and circulation.

items.title: Coronary Angiography
items.text: Angiography is done to identify the blocked heart artery quickly.

items.title: Primary Angioplasty (PCI) / Stenting
items.text: A blocked artery is opened using a balloon and stent to restore blood flow.

items.title: Thrombolysis
items.text: Clot-dissolving treatment is given to restore blood flow in time-sensitive heart emergencies.

items.title: ECMO / IABP Initiation
items.text: Advanced heart support is used to stabilise patients with severe cardiac failure or shock.

items.title: •	Pericardiocentesis
items.text: Fluid around the heart is drained to relieve pressure and stabilise circulation.

items.title: Temporary Pacing (TPI)
items.text: Temporary pacing is used to support dangerously slow heart rhythms.

items.title: Stroke Fibrinolysis
items.text: Time-sensitive clot treatment is used after urgent brain imaging in selected stroke cases.

items.title: Seizure Stabilisation (Emergency Seizure Care)
items.text: Seizures are controlled promptly to protect breathing and brain function, followed by evaluation of the cause.

items.title: External Ventricular Drain (EVD)
items.text: A drain is placed to reduce pressure in the brain in critical neurological situations.

items.title: Acute Abdomen Stabilisation
items.text: Urgent assessment and stabilisation are provided for severe abdominal pain, with timely imaging and surgical escalation.

items.title: GI Bleeding Stabilisation
items.text: Rapid stabilisation is provided for vomiting blood or blood in stool, with prompt coordination for definitive control of bleeding.

items.title: Bowel Obstruction Support
items.text: Decompression and stabilisation are initiated to reduce vomiting and abdominal distension, followed by surgical evaluation.

items.title: Wound Suturing / Laceration Repair
items.text: Wounds are cleaned and closed safely to control bleeding and reduce infection risk.

items.title: Abscess Drainage (I&D)
items.text: Localised infections are drained to relieve pain and control infection, with antibiotics when needed.

items.title: Pregnancy Emergency Stabilisation
items.text: Urgent pregnancy concerns are assessed quickly, with timely obstetric support for stabilisation.

items.title: Acute Bleeding / Severe Pelvic Pain Care
items.text: Immediate evaluation and stabilisation are provided, with escalation for urgent intervention when needed.

items.title: Emergency Vaginal Delivery Support
items.text: Rapid delivery support is provided when labour is advanced or urgent delivery is needed for mother or baby.

items.title: Emergency C-Section (LSCS)
items.text: An urgent C-section is performed when a safe delivery requires immediate surgical intervention.

items.title: Postpartum Haemorrhage Stabilisation
items.text: Heavy bleeding after delivery is managed quickly to stabilise the mother and prevent complications.

items.title: Poly-Trauma Resuscitation
items.text: Rapid stabilisation is provided for multiple injuries, focusing on airway, breathing and circulation.

items.title: Surgical Airway Insertion
items.text: An emergency airway is created when the usual airway methods cannot secure breathing.

items.title: Low Sugar / High Sugar Stabilisation
items.text: — Blood sugar is corrected safely with close monitoring to prevent complications.

items.title: High BP / Low BP Stabilisation
items.text: Blood pressure is stabilised promptly to protect the heart, brain and kidneys.

items.title: Emergency Dialysis Initiation
items.text: Dialysis is initiated to manage fluid overload and serious kidney-related emergencies.

items.title: Gastric Lavage
items.text: Stomach decontamination may be performed to reduce toxin absorption in poisoning cases.

items.title: Poison-Specific Antidote Administration
items.text: Specific antidotes are given to counter the effects of certain poisons.

items.title: Paediatric Emergency Stabilisation
items.text: Children receive quick assessment and stabilisation with age-appropriate monitoring and care.

items.title: Paediatric Breathing Support
items.text: Breathing support is provided early, including oxygen and ventilation when required.

items.title: Scope/Device-Guided Foreign Body Removal
items.text: Foreign bodies are removed safely using the right instruments to protect delicate tissues.

protocols.title: Protocol-based Response
protocols.subtitle: We follow a well-defined protocol to ensure fast, organised care from the moment the patient arrives to the time they are stabilised or admitted for further treatment

items.title: Trauma Protocol
items.heading: Coordinated Trauma Response
items.description: A structured, multi-disciplinary approach for multiple or severe injuries, focused on rapid stabilisation and timely definitive care.

items.title: Stroke Protocol
items.heading: Rapid Stroke Activation
items.description: Fast triage and urgent brain imaging to confirm stroke type, followed by timely treatment and specialist escalation as indicated.

items.title: Heart Attack & Cardiac Arrest Protocol
items.heading: Time-Critical Heart Response
items.description: Immediate ECG and resuscitation readiness with rapid cardiology activation to initiate treatment and stabilise the patient without delay.

items.title: Sepsis Protocol
items.heading: Early Sepsis Recognition & Treatment
items.description: Quick identification of infection-related deterioration with prompt tests and treatment initiation, supported by critical care when required.

items.title: Breathing Distress Protocol
items.heading: Rapid Breathing Support
items.description: Structured management for severe breathlessness, with oxygen support and escalation to NIV/ventilation when clinically needed.

items.title: Severe Allergy Protocol
items.heading: Immediate Allergy Emergency Care
items.description: Protocol-led treatment for severe allergic reactions, with airway circulation support and observation based on clinical risk.

items.title: Maternity Emergency Protocol
items.heading: Urgent Pregnancy Support
items.description: Rapid assessment and stabilisation of pregnancy-related emergencies, with timely obstetric support and safe escalation when required.

items.title: Paediatric Emergency Protocol
items.heading: Child-Focused Emergency Care
items.description: Rapid assessment and stabilisation for common childhood emergencies, with age-appropriate monitoring and specialist support when needed.

performance.title: Delivering Timely Emergency Care
performance.subtitle: Our emergency team ensures immediate medical attention around the clock.

items.question: When should I go to an emergency hospital?
items.answer: You should visit an emergency hospital if you have serious symptoms like chest pain, breathing trouble, stroke signs, high fever with confusion, heavy bleeding, or any major injury or sudden illness.

items.question: Are all emergency services available at Narayana Health hospitals?
items.answer: Yes. Narayana Health provides emergency services in all hospital at all its locations. These services are available day and night to treat critical medical problems without delay.

items.question: What happens at a hospital emergency department?
items.answer: When you arrive at a hospital emergency department, doctors and nurses check your condition quickly. You will be given treatment based on how serious your illness or injury is.

items.question: Does Narayana Health have trauma care hospital facilities?
items.answer: Yes. Narayana Health is a trusted trauma care hospital for treating accident injuries, head injuries, fractures, falls, and other serious conditions. Our team is trained to act fast in emergencies.

items.question: Who will treat me at an emergency care hospital?
items.answer: At an emergency care hospital, trained doctors, nurses, and support teams are available 24×7. They are supported by specialist experts across heart, brain, bone, and women’s health—such as cardiologists, neurologists, orthopaedic specialists, gynaecologists, urologists, gastroenterologists, nephrologists, and surgeons across specialties, to deliver the right care at the right time.

items.question: What is emergency medicine?
items.answer: Emergency medicine is the area of healthcare that treats urgent health problems. Doctors in this field are trained to give fast treatment for heart attacks, strokes, accidents, and other emergencies.

items.question: Do I need an appointment to visit a 24x7 emergency hospital?
items.answer: No, you do not need any appointment. A 24x7 emergency hospital is open all day and night. You can come anytime if you need quick medical help.

items.question: What type of support is given for accident care?
items.answer: Narayana Health provides full accident care, including first aid, tests & scans, emergency surgery, and ICU support. Our teams act quickly to help patients with injuries from accidents or falls.

items.question: Are accident care specialists available at all times?
items.answer: Yes. At our hospitals, experienced accident care specialists are available 24x7 to take care of patients who need urgent treatment after accidents or injuries.

items.question: Will I get ambulance help from the emergency hospital?
items.answer: Yes. Each emergency hospital at Narayana Health has 24x7 ambulance support with trained staff and equipment to bring patients safely to the hospital in an emergency.
